morning_starts.title: Matt's Big Breakfast
morning_starts.note: Small menu, big flavor, and a line that moves — get there before the sun means business.

morning_starts.title: Gallo Blanco Cafe
morning_starts.note: Huevos rancheros and strong coffee — fuel up here before the pavement starts radiating like a stovetop.

morning_starts.title: Otro Cafe
morning_starts.note: Patio's lovely at 7am, a furnace by 10 — plan accordingly, amigo.

morning_starts.title: Lola Coffee
morning_starts.note: Good espresso, better AC. Two things a desert morning demands.

morning_starts.title: Songbird Coffee & Tea House
morning_starts.note: A cozy nook for folks who like their caffeine with a side of quiet before the heat starts yelling.

morning_starts.title: Cartel Roasting Co.
morning_starts.note: Locally roasted, seriously caffeinated — the jolt you'll need before the 100-degree noon arrives.

morning_starts.title: La Purisima Bakery
morning_starts.note: Pan dulce that'll have you forgetting the thermometer already reads 95.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Echo Canyon Trail (Camelback Mountain)
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Go at sunrise or don't go at all — this rock doesn't care about your Instagram, it cares about heatstroke.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Piestewa Peak Summit Trail #300
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Steep, sweaty, and gorgeous before 8am; a suffer-fest after.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: South Mountain Park & Preserve
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Miles of trail and zero shade — bring more water than you think you need, then bring more.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Papago Park & Hole-in-the-Rock
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Red rocks, easy stroll, decent sunrise views without needing a search-and-rescue team.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Salt River Tubing
beach_lake_outdoor.note: The one outdoor activity where being drenched is the whole point — smart move in July.

beach_lake_outdoor.title: Riverbound Sports Paddle Co.
beach_lake_outdoor.note: Paddle the calm water before the afternoon sun turns the desert into an air fryer.

culture_history.title: Heard Museum
culture_history.note: World-class Native art, and it's air-conditioned — a two-for-one in this town.

culture_history.title: Musical Instrument Museum (MIM)
culture_history.note: Thousands of instruments, zero sunburn risk. My kind of afternoon.

culture_history.title: Phoenix Art Museum
culture_history.note: Wander the galleries slow; nobody's rushing you back out into that heat.

culture_history.title: Roosevelt Row Arts District
culture_history.note: Murals and galleries best walked at golden hour, not high noon — trust the cactus on this one.

culture_history.title: S'edav Va'aki Museum (formerly Pueblo Grande)
culture_history.note: A thousand-year-old village that figured out desert living long before swamp coolers existed.

culture_history.title: Rosson House Museum at Heritage Square
culture_history.note: Victorian charm in a town built on adobe and sunscreen — a nice historical detour.
culture_history.business: Rosson House Museum at Heritage Square

culture_history.title: Orpheum Theatre
culture_history.note: Gorgeous old bones and, crucially, indoor climate control.

shopping_browsing.title: Changing Hands Bookstore + First Draft Book Bar
shopping_browsing.note: Books and a bar under one roof — the smartest shelter-from-the-sun combo in the Valley.
shopping_browsing.business: Changing Hands Bookstore + First Draft Book Bar

shopping_browsing.title: Grassrootz Books & Juice Bar
shopping_browsing.note: Browse the shelves, sip something cold, avoid the sidewalk entirely.

shopping_browsing.title: Palabras Bilingual Bookstore
shopping_browsing.note: A cozy stop for readers, and blessedly out of direct sun.

shopping_browsing.title: Stinkweeds
shopping_browsing.note: Dig through vinyl in the AC while the asphalt outside hits 150 degrees.

shopping_browsing.title: Tracks in Wax
shopping_browsing.note: Record crates and shade — what more does a Tuesday need.

shopping_browsing.title: Retro Ranch
shopping_browsing.note: Vintage western wear, because you'll want a good hat out here regardless of the decade.

shopping_browsing.title: Biltmore Fashion Park
shopping_browsing.note: Upscale, shaded walkways — designed by someone who's clearly felt an August afternoon.

casual_lunch.title: Huarachis Taqueria
casual_lunch.note: Handmade huaraches that'll make you forget you're sweating through your shirt.

casual_lunch.title: Tacos Chiwas
casual_lunch.note: Chihuahua-style tacos worth the walk, even in shoes that are quietly melting.

casual_lunch.title: Asadero Norte de Sonora
casual_lunch.note: Sonoran-style grilling done right — carnivores, this is your stop.

casual_lunch.title: Nogales Hot Dogs
casual_lunch.note: Bacon-wrapped, borderland classic — a lunch that doesn't ask permission.

casual_lunch.title: Los Reyes de la Torta
casual_lunch.note: Tortas the size of your forearm, built for a proper midday refuel.

casual_lunch.title: The Original Carolina's Mexican Food
casual_lunch.note: A Phoenix institution — tortillas made fresh since before your AC unit was invented.

casual_lunch.title: The Fry Bread House
casual_lunch.note: James Beard-approved fry bread, and shaded tables — plan your visit around the shade, not the menu.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Bitter & Twisted Cocktail Parlour
happy_hour_drinks.note: Serious cocktails in a saloon that knows a thing or two about surviving dry heat.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Little Rituals
happy_hour_drinks.note: Small plates, sharp drinks — a solid hideout once the sidewalk stops being walkable.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Valley Bar
happy_hour_drinks.note: Downstairs bar, live music upstairs — one address, two ways to dodge the sun.

happy_hour_drinks.title: UnderTow
happy_hour_drinks.note: Tiki drinks that'll trick your brain into thinking you're somewhere with actual humidity.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Wren & Wolf
happy_hour_drinks.note: Handsome cocktails, handsome patio — enjoy the patio after 7pm, not before.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Wren House Brewing Company
happy_hour_drinks.note: Local beer, taproom shade — a desert-approved happy hour.

happy_hour_drinks.title: Arizona Wilderness DTPHX
happy_hour_drinks.note: Craft beer brewed by people who understand water conservation better than most.

dinner_casual.title: Beckett's Table
dinner_casual.note: Comfort food elevated just enough to feel like an occasion.

dinner_casual.title: The Gladly
dinner_casual.note: Reliable, unfussy, and open late enough for a post-sunset stroll over.

dinner_casual.title: Durant's
dinner_casual.note: Old-school Phoenix steakhouse — walk in through the kitchen, like the regulars do.

dinner_casual.title: The Stockyards
dinner_casual.note: Western steakhouse charm since the actual stockyards were, in fact, still yards.

dinner_casual.title: Tratto
dinner_casual.note: Housemade pasta from the Pizzeria Bianco family — reserve ahead, this one fills up.

dinner_casual.title: Valentine
dinner_casual.note: Neighborhood spot with a menu that changes more than the weather does, which is to say: never.

dinner_upscale.title: Steak 44
dinner_upscale.note: A steakhouse that means business, and the AC hits as hard as the ribeye.

dinner_upscale.title: Buck & Rider
dinner_upscale.note: Seafood in the middle of the desert — a small miracle, well executed.

dinner_upscale.title: First & Last
dinner_upscale.note: Sceney Italian with a wood-fired oven; dress like you mean it.

dinner_upscale.title: J&G Steakhouse at The Phoenician
dinner_upscale.note: Resort-level steak, resort-level views, resort-level AC.

dinner_upscale.title: Pizzeria Bianco
dinner_upscale.note: James Beard's favorite pizza in America, allegedly — the line outside makes the case for you.

dinner_upscale.title: Vincent on Camelback
dinner_upscale.note: French-Southwestern fusion from a Phoenix legend — book ahead, always.

dinner_romantic.title: Vincent on Camelback
dinner_romantic.note: Candlelight and a wine list built for slow evenings — the classic Phoenix date night.

dinner_romantic.title: Different Pointe of View
dinner_romantic.note: City lights below, dinner above — the view alone justifies the drive up the hill.

dinner_romantic.title: Christopher's at Wrigley Mansion
dinner_romantic.note: A mansion, a sunset, and a tasting menu — about as romantic as this desert gets.

dinner_romantic.title: T. Cook's at Royal Palms Resort and Spa
dinner_romantic.note: Mediterranean-inspired, resort-quiet — good for a proposal or a very sincere apology.
dinner_romantic.business: T. Cook's at Royal Palms Resort and Spa

dinner_romantic.title: Durant's
dinner_romantic.note: Red leather booths and low lighting since 1950 — old Phoenix romance, unbothered by trends.

dinner_romantic.title: Restaurant Progress
dinner_romantic.note: Intimate, seasonal, and dim enough to forget it's 108 outside.

nightlife.title: Crescent Ballroom
nightlife.note: Live music and a solid taco truck parked out front — Phoenix nightlife's best two-for-one.

nightlife.title: The Van Buren
nightlife.note: Big acts, good sound, and — bonus — it's indoors.

nightlife.title: Valley Bar
nightlife.note: Basement bar, upstairs venue, one very efficient building.

nightlife.title: Stand Up Live
nightlife.note: Comedy club for when you need to laugh at something other than the heat index.

nightlife.title: Bitter & Twisted Cocktail Parlour
nightlife.note: Late-night cocktails for people who take their whiskey seriously.

nightlife.title: Little Rituals
nightlife.note: A late-night hideout with drinks sharper than the desert air is dry.

nightlife.title: UnderTow
nightlife.note: Rum-forward and dim-lit — the closest this city gets to a tropical night out.

family_activities.title: Arizona Science Center
family_activities.note: Hands-on science, blessedly indoors — the kids won't even notice it's 110 outside.

family_activities.title: Musical Instrument Museum (MIM)
family_activities.note: A whole world of instruments under one climate-controlled roof.

family_activities.title: Desert Botanical Garden
family_activities.note: Go at dawn with the little ones — the cacti are patient, the sun is not.

family_activities.title: Salt River Tubing
family_activities.note: Float the river, splash the kids, survive July as a family unit.

family_activities.title: Papago Park & Hole-in-the-Rock
family_activities.note: Easy trails and a fun scramble up the rock — bring hats, bring water, then bring more water.

family_activities.title: Chase Field
family_activities.note: A retractable roof over a baseball diamond — someone in this city understands the assignment.

family_activities.title: S'edav Va'aki Museum (formerly Pueblo Grande)
family_activities.note: A gentle, educational stop that won't wear out little legs — or melt them.

rainy_day.title: Arizona Science Center
rainy_day.note: It never really rains here — the real enemy is July, and this place is the shelter.

rainy_day.title: Phoenix Art Museum
rainy_day.note: A full afternoon indoors, no sunscreen required.

rainy_day.title: Heard Museum
rainy_day.note: Rich history, cool galleries — a perfect dodge from either rain or, more likely, heat.

rainy_day.title: Musical Instrument Museum (MIM)
rainy_day.note: Hours of wandering without once stepping into direct sunlight.

rainy_day.title: Rosson House Museum at Heritage Square
rainy_day.note: A quiet historical tour, mercifully roofed.
rainy_day.business: Rosson House Museum at Heritage Square

rainy_day.title: Changing Hands Bookstore + First Draft Book Bar
rainy_day.note: When the sky finally does something interesting, come read about it instead.
rainy_day.business: Changing Hands Bookstore + First Draft Book Bar
